documents.title: AI Resources (incl. Generative AI Guidance for Privacy and Security)
documents.summary: IT Services page on AI risks, built-in AI tools in BGSU software, and tools for detecting or preventing student AI use. Mostly privacy and security advice for staff and students; it says student AI use on coursework is 'not ideal' but sets no rule.
documents.stance_why: A coded delegates, B coded permit. The page sets no rule for coursework: it says student AI use on assignments or tests 'is not ideal' (soft, not a ban), permits ChatGPT only as a tool-level data-protection condition, and points instructors to the Center for Faculty Excellence and to detection or lockdown tools they 'can' use. The decision about student use in a course is left to instructors, so delegates; the ChatGPT line is a rule about data settings, not a stance on teaching and learning.

units.why: Defines AI by quoting TechTarget: 'the simulation of human intelligence processes by machines'. A definition that sets what the page covers, so P61 and 'informs'.

units.why: States the page's purpose: 'to caution users on risks associated with using AI and to share resources to help detect AI use in coursework'. A preamble of purpose and scope, so P56.

units.resolution_why: A coded P50 / admin, B coded P65 / all. The sentence says formal project requests and technology reviews 'are required for implementation of any new AI tool'; it is a review gate for adopting tools (vetted tools), not a rule about vendor contracts or data sharing, so P50 fits and P65 does not. It binds the units that implement tools, so admin.

documents.stance_why: The guide says 'there are no campus-wide policies' and tells students to 'ask your instructor about their individual policy', handing the decision to instructors, so delegates.
